cards.text: The whole earth is under water, and the ark is floating on top (Genesis 7:18-19). Inside are Noah, the man God told to build it (Genesis 6:14), plus his family and the animals. But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark.

cards.question: God remembers Noah out on the water. What does He send over the earth?

cards.text: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens are closed, and the rain from the sky is held back. Like a 300-message group chat that FINALLY goes quiet.

cards.question: Once the rain is held back, the floodwaters are gone in a single day.

cards.text: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark comes to rest. You know that feeling when you've circled a parking lot for TEN minutes and a spot opens up?

cards.question: Where does the ark come to rest?

cards.text: The waters keep going down, month after month. Then on the first day of the tenth month, something besides water finally shows up out there.

cards.question: On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the ___ become visible.

cards.text: After forty days, Noah opens the window he made in the ark. Out goes a raven.

cards.question: The raven Noah sends out keeps flying back and forth until the waters dry up.

cards.text: Then Noah sends out a dove to see if the waters have gone down from the ground. My cookie cutter kid Minty is shaped like a dove and always checked on everybody, so this bird is basically family.

cards.question: The dove goes out on her first trip from the ark. What happens to her?

answers.text: She finds nowhere to land and returns
She stays out until the next morning
She builds a nest in a tree

cards.text: The waters still cover the surface of all the earth, so Noah reaches out his hand and brings her back inside the ark. A whole boat full of animals, and this man makes time for one little bird.
Noah waits seven more days and sends the dove out again. And this time, she comes back to him in the evening carrying something.

cards.question: The dove comes back to Noah in the evening. What is she carrying in her beak?
The dove's olive leaf is freshly plucked. So Noah knows the waters have ___.

cards.text: Noah waits seven MORE days and sends her out one more time. Friend, I can't even wait seven minutes for my oven to preheat.

cards.question: Noah sends the dove out a third time, and she comes back to him again.

cards.text: In Noah's six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, Noah removes the covering from the ark. Then he takes a look, like opening the oven door to check on a batch.

cards.question: Noah removes the covering from the ark and sees that the surface of the ground is ___.

cards.text: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth is fully dry. Then God speaks to Noah.

cards.question: Once the earth is fully dry, God tells Noah and his family to ___ the ark.
God tells Noah to bring out the birds, the livestock and everything that crawls. Why does God want them out?

answers.text: So they can spread out and multiply
So Noah can count every one
So the ark can be taken apart

cards.text: So out they come, Noah's family and every creature, kind by kind, like the whole office pouring out the door at five o'clock on a Friday. Then Noah builds an altar to the LORD.

cards.question: Noah offers burnt offerings on the altar. Which animals and birds does he take them from?

cards.text: The LORD smells the pleasing aroma. And He says something in His heart.

cards.question: The LORD says in His heart that He will never again curse the ground because of man.
The LORD says in His heart He will never again curse the ground because of man. What does He say about every inclination of man's heart?

answers.text: It is evil from his youth
It is pure from his youth
It is humble from his youth

cards.question: The LORD also says in His heart that someday He will again destroy all living creatures as He has done.

cards.text: The LORD goes on: as long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease. So every snooze button out there is fighting a losing battle, friend.
Then God blesses Noah and his sons, and He says to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth."
God says every creature will fear and dread them, and everything that lives and moves will be food for them, just as He gave the green plants. But there's one catch.

cards.question: The catch is that Noah's family must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.

cards.text: Then God says He will require the life of any man or beast by whose hand human blood is shed. He will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man.

cards.question: God says whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed. Why does God treat human life this seriously?

answers.text: God made mankind in His own image
Few people are left after the flood
Men must answer to their rulers

cards.text: And God comes right back around: be fruitful and multiply, spread out across the earth and multiply upon it. He opened this speech with be fruitful and multiply, and He's closing with it too.
Then God speaks to Noah and his sons again, and this one is BIG. He says He is now establishing His covenant with them.

cards.question: God's covenant here is only with Noah and his family, not with the animals that came out of the ark.
In His covenant, God promises that never again will all life be cut off. By what?

cards.text: Then God says this covenant comes with a sign, between Him and Noah's family and every living creature with them.

cards.question: God gives a sign of His covenant. What does He set in the clouds?

cards.text: Here's how it works. Whenever God forms clouds over the earth, and the rainbow appears in the clouds...

cards.question: Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, what does God say He will do?

cards.text: God says whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, He will see it and remember. Next time you see somebody pull over just to snap a picture of a rainbow, friend, they're onto something.

cards.question: God calls this the ___ covenant between God and every living creature on the earth.

cards.text: So God tells Noah one more time: this is the sign of the covenant He has established between Him and every creature on the earth. Hold that rainbow in your mind, friend, because Noah's story isn't finished yet.
